findings.reason: Every other topic manifest, including aktivitetspenger-soknad-topics.yml, has its own .github/workflows/deploy-*-topics.yml. No workflow references the new file, and build-and-deploy.yml:14 ignores changes under nais/topics/*. Lowered from high because the topics could still be applied by hand. Without that, deploying to a new environment leaves the three new streams with nothing to consume.
findings.claim: The new topic manifest is never deployed by any workflow, so the income-reporting topics may not exist where the streams run.
findings.evidence: No workflow references this manifest; every other topic manifest has a deployment workflow. build-and-deploy.yml excludes nais/topics/* and does not apply these resources, while AktivitetspengerInntektsrapporteringTopologyConfiguration immediately enables streams consuming the new topics.

findings.reason: Hibernate Validator only treats get/is/has methods as getters, and no custom getter strategy exists in src. So harOppgittInntekt() at OppgittInntekt.kt:12 and OppgittInntektForPeriode.kt:17 is never evaluated, and {} with null income passes @Valid. The same dead constraint already exists in the ungdomsytelse code this change copied.
findings.claim: @AssertTrue sits on harOppgittInntekt(), which is not a bean getter, so an empty oppgittInntekt passes validation.
findings.evidence: For oppgittInntekt: {}, arbeidstakerOgFrilansInntekt defaults to null. @AssertTrue annotates harOppgittInntekt(), which is not a bean property getter and is never explicitly called. Controller @Valid and InnsendingService.validator.validate() therefore do not evaluate this check; OppgittInntektForPeriode repeats the same ineffective constraint.

members.claim: An empty income object bypasses the declared required-income validation because the constraint annotates a non-getter method.

findings.reason: The order is real: registrer() at AktivitetspengerService.kt:100 runs before markerOppgaveSomLøst() at :102, and the latter throws when the call fails. But UngdomsytelseService.kt:135-137 uses the same order, so this looks like an accepted project pattern rather than a new defect. The duplicate cache also limits retries.
findings.claim: If marking the task complete fails after the Kafka publish, the report stays published but the task stays open, and a later retry can publish a duplicate.
findings.evidence: inntektrapportering() calls registrer() before markerOppgaveSomLøst(). KafkaProducerService completes executeInTransaction before registrer() returns. If the subsequent API call fails before updating the task, there is no recovery record or compensation. After the local duplicate cache expires, retrying publishes another message with fresh metadata before attempting task completion again.

members.claim: A task-completion failure after Kafka publication leaves a submitted report marked incomplete and allows retries to create duplicate reports.
